glossary.decision: Phase 6.2 T0 C4: controlled VI->EN expansion, no LLM, no translation API, never replaces the Vietnamese query
rules: An entry fires only when one of its Vietnamese triggers occurs in the question (word-boundary match, longest trigger first; matched words are consumed).
English terms are translations or accepted spelling/abbreviation variants of the trigger only: no added symptom, diagnosis, cause or intent.
Matching uses the question as written (NFC, lower case). Only when the question has NO Vietnamese diacritics is it matched against the accent-stripped triggers.
A term is a phrase (phraseto_tsquery) unless prefixed 'all:' (every word required, any order: plainto_tsquery).
UK and US spellings are both listed because the 'english' config stems them to different lexemes (behaviour/behavior).
Upper-case acronyms and letter+digit tokens in the question (ADHD, AAC, DSM-5, ADOS-2, M-CHAT-R/F, NDBI, ABA, WHO, SenITA) are passed through as English terms.

Development caveat: entries were written from the vocabulary of the 66 retrieval_eval_v1 questions (dev = test). Results on those questions are optimistic; a held-out question set is required before any claim of generalisation.
